To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PSA-NCANM is involved in LHRH migration in two ways.

polysialic acid (PSA) is necessary for the migration of a subset of luteinizing hormone releasing hormone (LHRN) neurons, that PSA expressed by vomeronasal nerves, and not by LHRH neurons, is required for the migration of these cells, and that PSA expressed by a specific vomeronasal branch is necessary for the normal positioning of a subset of LHRH neurons in the forebrain.
PSA-NC AM facilitates migration of LHRH neurons on VNN axons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the migration of the luteinizing hormone releasing hormone neurons from the olfactory placebo to the hypothalamus, which is essential for the development of reproductive functions.
the migration of the LHR H neurons from their origin in the olfactory placodes to the hypothalamus, where they synthesize the hormone that regulates gonadotropin secretion.
the role of PSA in the migration of LHRH neurons in the mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PSA-NCACM is not required for migration of LHRH neurons, but is a permissive factor that facilitates the migration of some of the cells along VNN tracts.
PSA-NC AM is a necessary but not sufficient factor for the migration of LHRH neurons along the VNN.
PSA-NCAm is required in a cell-autonomous fashion for the migration of a subset of LHRH neurons along the proximal Vnn tract.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PSA-NCAN is a permissive factor for migration of LHRH neurons along VNN axons.
the PSA-NCAM expressed by the NCAM-160 isoform, but not by NCAM-180, facilitates the migration of LHRH neurons on the PSA-NCM-140-positive VNN axons.
PSA-NCANM is not required to guide the migration of the majority of LHRH neurons but that it facilitates migration of a subpopulation of LHRH neuronal cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PSA-NCANM is not required for LHRH cell movement on the VNN, but it is required to guide the cells to a specific axonal branch.

polysialic acid is important for the migration of LHRH neurons, but the underlying mechanism may not be as simple as the presence of a polysialic acid ligand on axons that attracts the migrating cells.
PSA-NCAm is a necessary but not sufficient component in the guidance of migrating LHRh cells.
